quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I've been ____ for a new laptop for weeks, but I still haven't found the right one.
quests.hint: This is the -ing form used after 'have been' to show an ongoing search.
quests.explanation: "Have been looking" is present perfect continuous, showing a search that has continued over weeks.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The actor ____ won several awards is starring in the new film.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to a person and is the subject of the clause.
quests.explanation: "Who" refers to a person and is the subject of "won several awards," describing the actor.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: ____ she was exhausted, she still finished the marathon.
quests.hint: This word introduces a contrast and is followed by a full clause with a subject and verb.
quests.explanation: "Although" introduces a contrasting clause; "despite" would need a noun or -ing form instead.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The book ____ I borrowed from the library is due back next week.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to a thing — the book.
quests.explanation: "That" refers to things, correctly introducing this clause about the book.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I haven't seen my grandparents ____ last Christmas.
quests.hint: This word marks the starting point of a period, often used with the present perfect.
quests.explanation: "Since" marks a starting point in time, fitting a present perfect sentence like this one.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The hotel where we ____ last year has since been renovated.
quests.hint: This is the simple past tense, matching 'last year.'
quests.explanation: "Stayed" is the simple past tense, correctly matching the time marker "last year."

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The software was ____ by a small team of developers over two years.
quests.hint: This passive form follows 'was' to show the software received the action.
quests.explanation: "Developed" is the past participle needed after "was" to form the passive voice.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: ____ the deadline was tight, the team delivered the project on time.
quests.hint: This phrase introduces a contrasting clause with a subject and verb, unlike 'despite.'
quests.explanation: "Even though" introduces a full clause, unlike "despite," which needs a noun or -ing form.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: This restaurant is known ____ its authentic regional dishes.
quests.hint: This preposition follows 'known' when praising something a place is famous for.
quests.explanation: "Known for" is the correct collocation to describe what a restaurant is famous for.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The more I practice yoga, the ____ flexible I become.
quests.hint: This word completes the parallel comparative structure 'the more..., the ___...'
quests.explanation: "The more..., the more..." is a parallel structure showing two things increasing together.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I ended up buying the jacket ____ it was more expensive than I planned.
quests.hint: This phrase introduces a contrast and is followed by a full clause.
quests.explanation: "Even though" introduces a contrasting clause, showing the purchase happened despite the higher cost.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: This actress gave the performance ____ impressed critics the most this year.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to a thing — the performance — not a person.
quests.explanation: "That" refers to things like a performance, so it correctly introduces this clause.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I've been practicing English every day, so my speaking has really ____ this month.
quests.hint: This verb means 'gotten better,' fitting the result of regular practice.
quests.explanation: "Improved" means gotten better, fitting the result of daily practice.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ aware of the schedule change.
quests.hint: With 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the noun closest to it — here, 'students.'
quests.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb matches the nearer noun, "students," so "were" is correct.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I didn't realize how much I missed my family ____ I moved abroad.
quests.hint: This word shows the point when the realization happened, after moving away.
quests.explanation: "Until" shows the point when the realization happened, fitting this time clause.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: We need to leave now, or we ____ miss the train.
quests.hint: This modal completes a warning about a likely result if we don't leave now.
quests.explanation: "Will" shows a likely result, warning that missing the train is probable if we delay.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: This update fixes the bug ____ caused the app to crash.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to a thing — the bug — not a person.
quests.explanation: "That" refers to the bug, a thing, so it correctly introduces the relative clause here.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: Despite ____ well for the interview, she still felt nervous beforehand.
quests.hint: This -ing form follows 'despite,' which cannot be followed by a full clause.
quests.explanation: "Despite" must be followed by a noun or -ing form, so "preparing" is correct here.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I sent the soup back because it tasted far too salty ____ my liking.
quests.hint: This preposition completes the idiom 'too [adjective] for my liking.'
quests.explanation: "For my liking" is a fixed idiom meaning 'more than I prefer,' completed with "for."

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: After I finished all my chores, I ____ finally relax for the evening.
quests.hint: This modal shows a new ability gained after finishing the chores.
quests.explanation: "Could" shows the newly gained ability to relax after finishing all chores.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I didn't know about the sale, so I only bought one item ____ of several.
quests.hint: This word pairs with 'of' to show a substitution — one thing chosen over others.
quests.explanation: "Instead of" shows a substitution, meaning only one item was bought rather than several.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I have ____ seen such a moving performance in my life.
quests.hint: This frequency adverb means 'hardly ever,' fitting a performance that stood out as special.
quests.explanation: "Rarely" means hardly ever, fitting a performance memorable enough to stand out.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The medication should be taken ____ an empty stomach for the best results.
quests.hint: This preposition is part of a fixed phrase describing taking medicine without food.
quests.explanation: "On an empty stomach" is a fixed phrase meaning without food, common in medical instructions.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The results were ____ better than we had anticipated.
quests.hint: This word intensifies a comparative adjective and often pairs with 'better' or 'worse.'
quests.explanation: "Far" intensifies comparatives like "better," unlike "very" or "too," which don't fit comparatives.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The elderly couple ____ live next door have been married for fifty years.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to people — the couple next door.
quests.explanation: "Who" refers to people, correctly introducing a clause about the couple.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The tour guide recommended a restaurant ____ turned out to be closed on Mondays.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to a thing — the restaurant.
quests.explanation: "Which" refers to things, correctly introducing this clause about the restaurant.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I'd been using the same phone for years ____ I finally upgraded last month.
quests.hint: This word shows when a long-lasting situation finally ended.
quests.explanation: "Until" shows when the long use of the old phone ended, with the upgrade.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The proposal ____ several colleagues had reviewed was approved without changes.
quests.hint: This relative pronoun refers to a thing — the proposal.
quests.explanation: "That" refers to things like a proposal, correctly introducing this defining clause.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The chef explained that the sauce needed to simmer ____ at least two hours to develop rich flavor.
quests.hint: This word pairs with a length of time, like 'two hours.'
quests.explanation: "For" is used with a duration such as "two hours," unlike "since," which needs a starting point.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: I had only just sat down ____ the phone rang.
quests.hint: This word connects two closely timed past events, following 'had just...'
quests.explanation: "When" connects two closely timed past events, right after "had just sat down."
